summary: Join a fleet with only its invite code, bootstrapping Fabric trust through the external adapter

replay.detail: Existing claim history is retained. Pairing binds the new member's signed admission to its authenticated Fabric NodeID.

schema.detail: Pairing invitations carry a pinned gateway and one-use permit; signed join requests and admissions bind the Fabric NodeID. Ordinary HTTP invitations retain their existing transcript.

rules.detail: Pending Fabric identities receive no ordinary trust or grants. The adapter verifies signed st admission before atomic confirmation of client-only grants: st3/fleet/<fleet-id> and st3-client-v0. Reciprocal access uses the same set. Terminal access requires an explicit operator grant in static Fabric policy, which the adapter never edits.

compatibility.detail: Pairing requires coordinated st and st-fabric-adapter builds plus Fabric pairing and pairing_remote support. Existing non-pairing HTTP joins remain supported.

downtime.detail: No claim-store reset or history migration is required.

manual.detail: Run Fabric with --runtime-peers on both machines, install st-fabric-adapter, and run the adapter on the sponsor. Then use st fleet invite NAME and st fleet join CODE; no manual peer configuration is needed.

recovery.detail: Preserve adapter state across restarts. Expired, rejected or restart-lost pending attempts require a fresh invitation and never fall back to unverified trust. A replacement invite can retain the same machine name and verified member identity. Pruned historical permits terminate their journal without blocking other reconciliation or discarding unconfirmed identity fences.
